title: UV Disinfection System

introduction.definition: A UV disinfection reactor passes water through a stainless chamber close to ultraviolet lamps in quartz sleeves. UV-C light around 254 nm damages the DNA of bacteria, viruses and protozoa so they cannot reproduce. Automatic wipers keep the sleeves clean, and a sensor checks that the UV intensity is high enough.
applications: Wastewater effluent reuse and process water
key_points: Wipers and sensor keep dose assured
introduction.summary: A closed-vessel UV system disinfects water by passing it close to UV lamps housed in quartz sleeves. UV-C light inactivates bacteria, viruses and protozoa; automatic wipers keep sleeves clean and a sensor monitors intensity.

pressure.title: UV dose damages microbial DNA
pressure.description: UV-C light near 254 nm damages the DNA/RNA of bacteria, viruses and protozoa (Cryptosporidium, Giardia) so they cannot reproduce. Dose = intensity × exposure time (mJ/cm²; drinking water often ≈ 40 mJ/cm²). UV leaves no residual, so a small chlorine dose is often added for the distribution network; water UV transmittance and sleeve fouling control performance.

video_tutorials.title: UV Disinfection System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the UV Disinfection System.
A UV disinfection reactor passes water through a stainless chamber close to ultraviolet lamps in quartz sleeves.
UV-C light around 254 nm damages the DNA of bacteria, viruses and protozoa so they cannot reproduce.
Automatic wipers keep the sleeves clean, and a sensor checks that the UV intensity is high enough.
Typical applications include drinking water (especially for Cryptosporidium/Giardia); wastewater effluent reuse and process water.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the UV Disinfection System works.
Water enters the reactor chamber.
Lamps emit UV-C through quartz sleeves.
Microorganisms receive the UV dose as they pass.
Wipers clean the sleeves periodically.
The sensor and panel confirm intensity.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
UV-C light near 254 nm damages the DNA/RNA of bacteria, viruses and protozoa (Cryptosporidium, Giardia) so they cannot reproduce.

video_tutorials.title: UV Disinfection System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the UV Disinfection System.
Check UV intensity and alarms.
Inspect wipers; clean sleeves if needed.
Replace lamps (≈ 9,000 – 16,000 h).
Watch for low uv intensity: alarm, low sensor reading. Common cause: fouled sleeves, aged lamps, low uvt.
Watch for broken sleeve: water in lamp, trip. Common cause: thermal shock, impact.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
